title: MARION & DOMINIC — Master Game Skeleton
corePromise: Every story day is lived. The primary experience is continuous photorealistic interactive video driven by persistent world state; phone, agenda, dressing, memories and spontaneous visio are diegetic layers around it.
nonNegotiables: Start in Nîmes in May 1998 with Marion living an ordinary morning before Dominic enters her life.
Dominic is autonomous and is never summoned by a player button.
Day 1 contains a Dominic encounter in the day, but its exact timing, place and circumstances are resolved by the hidden director from plausible situations.
Every calendar day exists and advances through morning, midday, afternoon, evening and night; quiet days are still lived rather than skipped by default.
Video is the primary gameplay surface, not decoration. Marion may be visible on camera; scenes may show Marion and Dominic together.
Choices appear at natural dramatic beats and update persistent state rather than merely selecting a pre-rendered branch.
Phone/messages/calls/visio/agenda/dressing/memories can interrupt or overlay the current lived scene.
Outfit, age, appearance, relationships, promises, conflicts, locations and memories persist into later generated scenes.
Replay must vary while chronology, causality and canon remain coherent.
No generated media becomes live solely because generation succeeded; identity and visual quality gates are mandatory.

timeModel.rule: Actions consume story time. NPC schedules and hidden events advance while Marion acts, waits, travels, ignores a call or sleeps.
timeModel.sleep: Night resolution closes the day, writes memories/consequences, advances calendar, schedules pending world events and prepares likely next-day media.

worldState.relationships: Per pair: familiarity, trust, attraction, affection, tension, conflict, intimacy, commitments, boundaries, unresolvedTopics. Values influence possibilities but never expose gamey meters in the main UI.

dayLoop.purpose: Enter the exact persistent state inherited from the previous night.
Play continuous video beats of ordinary life and active story events.
Allow autonomous SMS, calls, visio, invitations and world events without stopping the world.
At natural beats, expose a small set of intentions plus contextual/freeform interaction where supported.
Update time, memories, relationships, schedules and hidden consequences.
Hidden director chooses the next plausible beat from state, schedules, canon, anti-repeat and run seed.
Prepare likely video continuations before the current segment ends.
Resolve the day and seed tomorrow without resetting state.

narrativeScale.day: Dense lived timeline with ordinary beats, encounters, communications, travel, choices and surprises.
narrativeScale.week: Schedules, recurring habits, unresolved conversations, invitations and consequences.
narrativeScale.month: Relationship evolution, social arcs, changing routines, seasonal events and medium-term consequences.
narrativeScale.year: Era progression, birthdays, work/life changes and major relationship/life possibilities.
narrativeScale.multiYear: Dating/couple/marriage/pregnancy/children and other life states are conditional outcomes, never forced menu milestones.

eventSystem.eligibility: An event is eligible only when chronology, location, participant availability, knowledge, memories, relationship state and exclusions all agree.
eventSystem.selection: Hidden director scores eligible events for plausibility, continuity, pacing, novelty and character autonomy; player never sees hidden candidate lists.

fixedTruths: Marion begins at home in Nîmes in May 1998.
Marine can contact Marion during the morning.
Dominic is not known/contactable at launch.
Marion lives her morning and leaves/acts according to player choices.
Marion encounters Dominic during Day 1, but not on launch and not via a Dominic button.
variable: whether contact details are exchanged immediately or later
day1.afterEncounter: Ordinary life continues. Dominic becomes an autonomous world actor; future contact depends on what actually happened.

videoRuntime.scene: A scene is a continuity chain of beats sharing location/time/wardrobe/emotional context.
videoRuntime.prefetch: While beat A plays, generate/cache the most plausible continuations B/C/D. Choice selects an already-ready continuation when possible; unused clips can be retained only if continuity-compatible.
videoRuntime.failure: Reject candidate, retry with adjusted motion/camera/model/seed; never silently publish a failed identity candidate.

uiContract.principle: Video owns the screen. Interface appears only when useful and should feel diegetic/minimal.
uiContract.main: Full-screen video with discreet time/place context; no permanent heavy HUD.
uiContract.choices: Appear at natural pause/beat, then recede.
uiContract.phone: Overlay/physical-device experience for messages, calls, gallery and spontaneous incoming visio.
uiContract.visio: Front-camera grammar, direct gaze, phone itself invisible unless the shot intentionally shows Marion holding it.
uiContract.dressing: Player chooses available outfit; selection writes currentOutfitId and becomes mandatory continuity for generated media.
uiContract.agenda: Shows what Marion knows, not omniscient hidden NPC schedules.
uiContract.memories: Player-facing traces of lived events; hidden causal memory remains richer.

directorRules: Never expose hidden future events in choice wording.
Never teleport Dominic into a scene because the player wants him there.
NPCs can be busy, late, unavailable, elsewhere or acting independently.
Choices express Marion's intention; outcomes depend on world state and other characters.
Quiet beats are allowed and necessary for realism.
Major events can reconverge structurally but must retain path-specific memories and consequences.
Generate only what must be seen; preserve deep state separately from video.

implementation.migration: Keep current new-game-shell logic as functional source material, but rebuild presentation against the validated visual mockup. Existing story graph becomes Day-1 authored seed content under this master skeleton.
nextMilestones: M1: canonical schema + persistent world state + exact day clock
M2: Day 1 complete playable graph from 09:12 through sleep, with encounter resolved during the day
M3: interactive video player capable of seamless beat chaining and prefetch
M4: MonIA Video Engine V3 adapter + candidate/quality/cache lifecycle
M6: week/month/year generators constrained by authored canon and persistent consequences
M7: rebuild screens pixel-close to the original validated mockup
